name: og-05-environmental-to-internal-bioenergetics
title: Owning Its Energy
question: Can selection move from externally imposed gradients toward internally maintained electrochemical states (catalytic ion transport then pumping)?
hypothesis: When membrane permeability, Na+/H+ coupling and catalyst efficiency vary under selection, systems with increasing internal gradient generation win on throughput + persistence — but only if membranes stay sufficiently leaky (Sojo constraint).
objective: Allow catalytic ion transport and active pumping; test whether selection favors internalized gradient generation.
proposed_models_methods: evolutionary control loop over membrane parameters

conditions.name: reproducibility
conditions.expr: solver and db and seed and scenario recorded

behavior_tests.name: sojo-constraint-weak-pump-collapses
behavior_tests.description: Discriminating (Sojo 2014): a weak pump cannot internalize, so when the external gradient collapses the lineage goes extinct — only sufficiently efficient pumps survive the transition.

pass_if.detail: the weak-pump control collapses (survivors ~0) where the efficient pump persists

behavior_tests.name: energy-cost-accounted
behavior_tests.description: Membrane-maintenance energy is outweighed by benefit in the surviving population (net-positive free-energy flux).

literature_anchors.expectation: LUCA-like cells can use proton gradients only if membranes remain sufficiently leaky
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Met by the real replicator selection loop — the survival Decision map over (pump efficiency × gradient floor) is bounded by the Sojo cost line (η ≈ 0.30): efficient pumps internalize and persist (~94% of the grid survives) while weak pumps collapse at the gradient transition.

claim: Survival off a collapsing gradient is a bounded REGION of (pump catalyst efficiency × gradient floor), mapped by a real replicator sweep — a lineage persists either by riding a floor that never falls too far OR by internalizing gradient generation, but internalizing only pays above the Sojo cost line (η ≈ 0.30). At the operating point an efficient pump internalizes (pump fraction 0→0.95) and survives while a weak pump collapses — the Sojo-2014 leaky-membrane constraint on bioenergetic internalization.

findings.statement: As the external geochemical gradient declines over the run, replicator selection drives the population from externally-driven (pump fraction ~0) to internalized gradient generation (pump fraction ~0.95) while persisting — the bioenergetic internalization is an evolutionary outcome, not a scripted upgrade.

evidence.observed: internalization 0.00 -> 0.95; survivors 1.0 at the collapsed gradient

findings.explanation: BioenergeticSelectionProcess replicator dynamics over a (permeability × pump) strategy grid with a Sojo leaky-membrane fitness; the declining gradient flips the winning strategy from leaky-external to tight-pump.

findings.statement: A weak pump cannot internalize — when the external gradient collapses, the weak-pump lineage goes extinct (survivors → 0) while the efficient-pump lineage persists. Internalization is only viable with a sufficiently efficient pump (the Sojo leaky-membrane constraint).

evidence.observed: efficient survivors 1.0 vs weak-pump survivors 0.0 at collapsed gradient

findings.explanation: Below a pump-efficiency threshold the internal-pump flux cannot beat its cost against the lost external coupling, so no strategy clears the survival floor.

findings.statement: Survival off the collapsing gradient is a bounded REGION, not two representative runs: the native (pump catalyst efficiency × gradient floor) Decision map survives at 185/196 points (~94%), with the low-floor / low-efficiency corner going extinct. The Sojo cost line (η ≈ 0.30 — where internal pumping clears its maintenance cost plus the survival floor) marks the internalize-or-die boundary, and internalization (pump fraction > 0.5) fills the efficient interior where the lineage truly OWNS its energy rather than riding the residual external gradient.

evidence.observed: 185/196 (94%) survive over (catalyst_efficiency 0.05–1.3 × gradient_floor 0.005–0.35); Sojo cost line η≈0.30; internalization 0.009–0.949 across the grid; operating point (η=1.0, floor=0.02) deep inside

findings.explanation: The bioenergetic_survival_map sweeps the real replicator loop under the declining gradient and reduces each point to the surviving fraction + the survives PASS mask; the Sojo efficiency floor is read from the selection process config ((survival_threshold + c_pump + c_base)/k_int). Rendered as the survival landscape + internalization map (Decision view).
findings.next_action: Sweep decline_rate / alternative collapse scenarios to test how the survival region deforms with the speed of gradient loss (og-05b).

findings.statement: Accounting the free energy by SOURCE (not just the net flux) shows the useful disequilibrium shifting from the external geochemical gradient to internally maintained power as the environment declines — the external share of the useful free energy peaks near ~82% early in the run, then collapses to ~1% as the gradient falls while the population persists. The organism comes to "own" its energy: the geochemical gradient becomes a resource it taps, not the scaffold that organizes it.

evidence.observed: external share of useful free energy peaks ~82% then falls to ~1% as external pmf 0.40 → 0.02 V; survivors 1.0, internalization → 0.95

findings.explanation: The selection process emits the population-mean provenance breakdown (external tap k_ext·pmf·P vs internal pump k_int·pump·eff·(1−P) vs maintenance cost); rendered as the stacked energy-provenance trajectory + the gradient-dependence curve (Mechanism view).

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces the Sojo-2014 constraint — internalization is viable only with a sufficiently efficient pump; a weak pump collapses at the transition.

explanatory_gain.basis: The evolutionary control loop explains both the internalization transition and its Sojo-bounded failure mode from the leaky-membrane fitness.

limitations: Coarse-grained deterministic replicator dynamics with calibrated couplings; not a wrapped ALife/MD engine.

The survival map fixes a single gradient-decline scenario (v_start 0.40, decline_rate 0.01); only efficiency × floor are swept, so the sensitivity to the speed/shape of the collapse is not yet mapped.

resolved_uncertainties: Selection can internalize gradient generation as the external gradient falls, bounded by the Sojo leaky-membrane constraint.
The pump-efficiency threshold is now mapped — the Sojo cost line (η ≈ 0.30) bounds a ~94% survival region of (efficiency × floor).
remaining_uncertainties: How the survival region deforms with the speed/shape of the gradient collapse (decline_rate is held fixed in the current map).

followup_study_proposals.rationale: Sweep decline_rate / alternative collapse scenarios to test how the survival region and the Sojo boundary shift with the speed of gradient loss.
